heads.la: CAPITULUM PRIMUM De differentia mundanae theologiae atque divinae et de demonstrationibus earumdem.
heads.en: CHAPTER ONE On the difference between worldly and divine theology, and on the demonstrations of each.

heads.la: CAPITULUM II. Quae sit materia hierarchiarum, et dispositio earum.
heads.en: CHAPTER II. What is the subject-matter of the hierarchies, and their arrangement.
CHAPTER III. On the three hierarchies

heads.la: CAPITULUM IV. Quare theologiam assumpsit tractandam Dionysius Areopagites postquam susceperat fidem catholicam.
heads.en: CHAPTER IV. Why Dionysius the Areopagite undertook to treat of theology, after he had received the catholic faith.

heads.la: CAPITULUM V. Quid sit hierarchia et dispositio illius et exordium.
heads.en: CHAPTER V. What a hierarchy is, and its arrangement and origin.

heads.la: LIBER SECUNDUS. Sequuntur tituli XV capitulorum coelestis sive angelicae hierarchiae divi Dionysii Areopagitae ad Timotheum; post quos singulorum capitulorum apponetur secundum Joannem Scotum littera; et post litteram, Hugonis nostri expositio.
heads.en: BOOK TWO. There follow the titles of the fifteen chapters of the celestial or angelic hierarchy of the blessed Dionysius the Areopagite, to Timothy; after which the text of each several chapter will be set down according to John Scotus; and after the text, the exposition of our Hugh.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI I. Quod divina illuminatio secundum bonitatem varie impraevisa proveniens, manet simpla; et non hoc solum sed et unificat illuminata.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER I. That the divine illumination, coming forth variously unforeseen according to goodness, remains simple; and not this only, but it also unifies the things illumined.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI II: Quod pulchre divina et coelestia etiam per dissimilia symbola manifestantur.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER II: That divine and heavenly things are beautifully manifested even through dissimilar symbols.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI III. Quid est hierarchia et quae per hierarchiam utilitas.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER III. What the hierarchy is, and what the benefit is through the hierarchy.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI IV. Quid significat angelorum cognominatio.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER IV. What the appellation of the angels signifies.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI V Quare omnes coelestes essentiae communiter angeli dicuntur, et specialiter proprias, praeterquam primi et ecundi ordinum habent agnominationes.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER V Why all the heavenly essences are commonly called angels, and specially have their own proper appellations, except those of the first and second orders.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI VI. Quae sit prima coelestium essentiarum dispositio: quae media, et quae ultima.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER VI. What is the first arrangement of the celestial essences: what the middle, and what the last.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI VII. De seraphim et thronis, hoc est de prima angelorum hierarchia.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER VII. On the seraphim and thrones, that is, on the first hierarchy of the angels.

heads.la: LIBER SEPTIMUS. Expositio in reliquam partem capitis septimi divi Dionysii Areopagitae de coelesti hierarchia, cujus littera praemissa est.
heads.en: BOOK SEVEN. Exposition of the remaining part of the seventh chapter of the divine Dionysius the Areopagite on the celestial hierarchy, the text of which has been set out above.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI VIII: De dominationibus, et potestatibus, et de media eorum hierarchia.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER VIII: On the dominations, and the powers, and on their middle hierarchy.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI IX: De principatibus, archangelis et angelis, et de ultima eorum hierarchia.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER IX: On the principalities, archangels, and angels, and on their last hierarchy.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI X. Synagogae angelicae ordinationis repetitio.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER X. A recapitulation of the ordering of the angelic synagogue.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI XI. Quare omnes coelestes essentiae communiter virtutes coelestes nominantur.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER XI. Why all the celestial essences are commonly named celestial virtues.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI XII. Quare secundum homines hierarchiae angeli vocantur.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER XII. Why hierarchies according to men are called angels.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI XIII. Quare a seraphim dicitur purgatus fuisse propheta Isaias.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER XIII. Why the prophet Isaiah is said to have been purged by a seraph.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI XIV. Quid significat traditus angelicus numerus.
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER XIV. What the handed-down angelic number signifies.

heads.la: TITULUS CAPITULI XV. Quae sunt formativae angelicarum virtutum imagines, et quae deinde, id est et reliqua?
heads.en: TITLE OF CHAPTER XV. What are the formative images of the angelic virtues, and what next, that is, and the rest?

headnotes.la: …i majestatis facti sunt, per partes, et divisiones, et gradus, et ordines distributum est, ab eo descendens et respiciens ad eum, et sub eo ordinatum qui fons et causa est omnium, et principium primum
headnotes.en: … majesty, through parts, and divisions, and degrees, and orders — descending from him and looking back to him, and ordered beneath him who is the fount and cause of all things, and the first beginning

headnotes.la: …it ad congregantis Patris unitatem, et deificam simplicitatem. Etenim ex ipso omnia, et in ipsum [n: (Rom. XI)]*, *ut divinum ait verbum. Ergo Jesum invocantes paternum lumen, quod est quod verum quod
headnotes.en: …ifying simplicity. For from him are all things, and unto him [n: (Rom. XI)]*, *as the divine word says. Therefore, calling upon Jesus, the paternal light, that which is, that which is true, that which

headnotes.la: …rticipationis summum bonum contemplari potest. Ideoque theologiam convenienter ex omni specie, et forma, et qualitate sensibili invisibilium significatione conformare. Et hic sensus est primi capituli
headnotes.en: …plated. And therefore it is fitting for theology to conform, out of every appearance and form and sensible quality, to the signification of invisible things. And this is the sense of the first chapter

headnotes.la: In hoc ergo probat, quod omne bonum a summo bono est. Post hoc subjungit, quod omne bonum ad summum bonum conversionem habet, et reductionem, et finem
headnotes.en: In this, therefore, he proves that every good is from the highest good. After this he adds that every good has its conversion, and its leading-back, and its end toward the highest good

headnotes.la: …a summo bono est, et omne bonum ad summum bonum est; ab illo enim accipimus, quod cum illo unum sumus; nec esset in nobis, quo respiceremus ad illum, nisi prius quod suum est, nostrum fieret per illum
headnotes.en: …good is toward the highest good; for from it we receive that we are one with it; nor would there be in us anything by which we might look toward it, unless first what is its own became ours through it

headnotes.la: …n est ipsum, quod nos illuminat, ut ex ipso sint omnia, et in ipsum; quae principium subsistendi accipiunt ab ipso, et finem consummationis in ipso, sicut divinum verbum per Paulum apostolum, testatur
headnotes.en: …that from it are all things and unto it; things which receive the beginning of their subsistence from it, and the end of their consummation in it, as the divine word through Paul the apostle testifies

headnotes.la: …orum traditiones, quae et ipsa ad luminanda corda hominum a Patre tradita sunt, possit et veraciter agnoscere, et digne narrare coelestium spirituum invisibiles illuminationes, et dispositiones sacras
headnotes.en: …wn by the Father for the illuminating of the hearts of men — he may be able both truly to recognize and worthily to narrate the invisible illuminations and sacred dispositions of the celestial spirits

headnotes.la: ac si diceret: Omnis quidem illuminatio a Patre est, sed sine Jesu mediatore nulla illuminatio haberi potest
headnotes.en: as if he said: Every illumination indeed is from the Father, but without Jesus the mediator no illumination can be had

headnotes.la: nos, qui illuminari poscimus,
headnotes.en: we, who ask to be illuminated,

headnotes.la: ut scilicet illuminari mereamur. Deinde sequitur de ipso Jesu Christo, quod est,
headnotes.en: namely that we may merit to be illuminated . Then there follows, concerning Jesus Christ himself, that it is

headnotes.la: pro eo quod dicere debuerat, qui est paternum lumen, ad sequentem dictionem relatio facta est, quod est paternum lumen. Vel
headnotes.en: instead of what he ought to have said, "who is the paternal light," the reference has been made to the following expression, "which is the paternal light." Or,

headnotes.la: …a, quae lumina sunt non ex eo quod sunt, sed ex eo quod acceperunt. Quod etiam lumen verum subauditur est lumen; quoniam ex eo quod est, lucet, et non solum sibi lucet, sed etiam alios illuminat. Quod
headnotes.en: …they have received. For which phrase "true light" — the word "light" too is understood — because from that which it is, it shines, and it shines not only for itself, but also illuminates others. Which

headnotes.la: …m est, per carnem, et facta est lumen in testa, ut illuminaret nos, et assuefaceret ad majus lumen, et perduceret ad principale lumen. Sed et ita accessum habuimus per Jesum ad principale lumen Patrem
headnotes.en: …vessel, that it might illuminate us, and accustom us to the greater light, and lead us through to the principal light. But thus also we have had access through Jesus to the principal light, the Father

headnotes.la: Hoc est, quod sequitur
headnotes.en: This is what follows

headnotes.la: … spirituum coelestium principatus sacros et potestates (qui nobis, nisi per Scripturae sacrae traditiones manifestarentur, invisibiles omnino essent et incogniti), consideremus. Hoc est enim, quod ait
headnotes.en: …its, that is, of the celestial spirits (which, unless they were made manifest to us through the traditions of Holy Scripture, would be altogether invisible and unknown to us). For this is what he says

headnotes.la: sive quantum possumus. Parvum est enim nostrum posse, et exiguum ad tantarum rerum magnitudinem
headnotes.en: or as far as we can. For our ability is small and scanty for the magnitude of such great things

headnotes.la: Sequitur
headnotes.en: There follows

headnotes.la: …m similitudinemque reformet. Propterea cognita ex sacris divini eloquii traditionibus coelestium spirituum claritate, qualiter hanc cognitionem summi luminis contemplatio subsequatur, ostendit, dicens
headnotes.en: … Therefore, the brightness of the celestial spirits being known from the sacred traditions of the divine oracle, he shows how the contemplation of the highest light follows upon this knowledge, saying

headnotes.la: … contemplatam, ad divini Patris claritatem illuminamur; quia et ipsa nobis angelorum claritas a claritate Patris per eos in nos descendente ex sacri eloquii revelatione manifestatur. Hoc est, quod ait
headnotes.en: … because the brightness of the angels itself too is made manifest to us, from the revelation of the sacred oracle, by the brightness of the Father descending through them into us. This is what he says

headnotes.la: Hoc est, quod sequitur
headnotes.en: This is what follows

headnotes.la: Sequitur

headnotes.en: …y from it: and so then each one, the more they approach, the more they receive; and the more they withdraw, the less they receive. Yet all receive; each one according to his part. This is what he says

headnotes.la: …liter se extendit, quia tamen ad omnes se extendit, et omnibus se infundit, omnes illuminat, et lumina esse facit ex lumine suo, ac per hoc unum esse facit, sicut ipse unus est. Et hoc est, quod dicit
headnotes.en: …nds itself to all, and pours itself into all, illuminates all, and makes them to be lights from its own light, and through this makes them to be one, just as it itself is one. And this is what he says

headnotes.la: Sequitur

headnotes.en: …y the study of reading or meditation is, as it were, only an image of that full and perfect knowledge which we shall afterward draw from the contemplation that is to come. Whence the Apostle also says

headnotes.la: Sequitur

headnotes.en: Again understand, our mind judging the orders of dispositions

headnotes.en: There follows

headnotes.la: …io Christi veritas non est, quia figura est. Nam et mortem Christi, et resurrectionem figuram esse, et imaginem esse, et similitudinem, et sacramentum, et exemplum Apostolus manifeste declarat, dicens
headnotes.en: …th, because it is a figure. For that both the death of Christ and the resurrection are a figure, and are an image, and a likeness, and a sacrament, and an example, the Apostle plainly declares, saying

headnotes.la: Et apostolus Petrus dixit
headnotes.en: And the apostle Peter said

headnotes.la: …xemplum fuit ut justitiae vivamus. Nunquid ideo veritas non fuit? ergo Christus vere mortuus non est, et vere non surrexit, si mors ejus, vel resurrectio vera non fuit. Absit! Nam de ipso scriptum est
headnotes.en: …hat we might live to justice. Was it therefore not truth? Then Christ did not truly die, and did not truly rise again, if his death, or resurrection, was not true. God forbid! For of him it is written

headnotes.la: …is et vinum principalis substantia est. Et proponitur species ex principali substantia refectionis, ut in ea sumatur, et per eum significetur veritas corporis et sanguinis, sicut ipse testatur, dicens
headnotes.en: … And the appearance is set forth from the principal substance of refreshment, that in it may be taken, and through it may be signified, the truth of the body and blood, as he himself testifies, saying

headnotes.la: Quae tamen corporis et sanguinis sumptio, quod sola sine spirituali effectu salutem non conferat, ipse idem Salvator manifesstat, dicens
headnotes.en: Yet that this taking of the body and blood, alone and without a spiritual effect, does not confer salvation, the same Savior himself manifests, saying

headnotes.la: Sequitur
headnotes.en: There follows

headnotes.la: Postquam quaedam, exempli gratia, ad ostendendam visibilium ad invisibilia similitudinem proposuit, nunc generaliter de toto concludit, dicens
headnotes.en: After he had set forth certain things, by way of example, to show the likeness of visible things to invisible, now he concludes generally about the whole, saying

headnotes.la: …m intelligentiam interpretemur. Quia enim dixerat invisibilia quaedam per eas quae determinatae sunt visibiles imagines, demonstrari, nunc generalem de ipsis invisibilibus sententiam subjungit, dicens
headnotes.en: …use he had said that certain invisible things are demonstrated through those visible images which are determinate, now he subjoins a general sentence concerning the invisible things themselves, saying

headnotes.la: Sequitur
headnotes.en: There follows

headnotes.la: id est divinitatem, quae nobis est corrationalis, id est congrua vel apta. Congruum enim est ut per ea, quae nota sunt nobis, divinorum participes efficiamur,
headnotes.en: that is, divinity, which is to us co-rational, that is, congruous or apt. For it is congruous that through those things which are known to us we should be made partakers of divine things

headnotes.la: quasi diceret: Quia humanus animus non potest de invisibilibus erudiri, nisi per visibilia et cognita, ac cognata sibi, igitur
headnotes.en: as if he were saying: Because the human mind cannot be instructed concerning invisible things save through visible things, and things known and akin to it, therefore

headnotes.la: id est Deus, a quo omnis perfectio initium habet, sicut in ipso consummationem capit, et finem sola gratia et misericordia, ut nos ad suam cognitionem revocaret, et similitudinem reformaret;
headnotes.en: …t is, God, from whom all perfection has its beginning, as in him it takes its consummation and end — by grace and mercy alone, that he might call us back to his own knowledge, and reform his likeness;

headnotes.la: id est angelicas potestates;
headnotes.en: that is, the angelic powers;

headnotes.la: …sit illis et in dignitate conformis, et in ministerio divino consimilis, servata in nobis similitudine deiformis earum sanctificationis, ut simus similes sanctificationi earum quae Deo conformes sunt,
headnotes.en: …mable to them in dignity, and like them in divine ministry, the deiform likeness of their sanctification being preserved in us, that we may be like the sanctification of them who are conformed to God,

headnotes.la: id est secundum possibilitatem nostram, hoc est quantum similes esse possumus, qui homines, et mortales, et peccato adhuc obnoxii sumus;
headnotes.en: that is, according to our possibility, that is, as far as we are able to be like — we who are men, and mortal, and still liable to sin;

headnotes.la: invisibiles spiritus, qui nobis incogniti erant, sensibilibus imaginibus, ut per nota incognita disceremus. Et hanc descriptionem fecit
headnotes.en: the invisible spirits, who were unknown to us, by sensible images, that through the known we might learn the unknown. And this description he made

headnotes.la: id est in sacri eloquii descriptionibus: quae compositiones, et figuras, et similitudines proponunt nobis ad invisibilium demonstrationem. Et hoc ideo fecit,
headnotes.en: that is, in the descriptions of the sacred word: which compositions set forth to us both figures and likenesses for the demonstration of invisible things. And this he did for this reason,

headnotes.la: hoc est per visibilia ad invisibilia. Et ut nos etiam reduceret et
headnotes.en: that is, through visible things to invisible things. And that he might also lead us back and

headnotes.la: id est de figuris sacris et sacrarum rerum figuris;
headnotes.en: that is, from sacred figures and the figures of sacred things;

headnotes.la: id est in simplices et spiritales excellentias cognoscendas
headnotes.en: that is, into the simple and spiritual excellences to be known

headnotes.la: …ndum veritatem supercoelestia, et divina spectacula. Sed itaque et hoc intelligere oportet: Nihil eorum, quae sunt, esse universaliter boni participatione privatum: siquidem, ut eloquiorum Veritas ait
headnotes.en: …use thus base. But so this too it behooves to understand: That nothing of those things which are, is universally deprived of the participation of the good: since indeed, as the Truth of the words says

headnotes.la: … verborum. Hoc enim introducendis primum magis conveniens est: praecipue quia illa, quae disserenda censuimus, magna nimis, et supra nostram possibilitatem agnoscimus. Titulus secundi capituli hic est
headnotes.en: … who are to be introduced: especially because those things which we judged were to be discussed we recognize to be exceedingly great, and above our possibility. The title of the second chapter is this

headnotes.la: Pudice temperat assertionem suam, ut prudentem decet; nec in rebus excellentibus, et a sensu humano remotis ultra hominis possibilitatem praesumere videtu, dicens
headnotes.en: Modestly he tempers his assertion, as befits a prudent man; nor in excellent matters, and remote from the human sense, does he seem to presume beyond man's possibility, saying

headnotes.la: …ui viderat, et sciebat. Sed servavit modestiam dictionis, ut haec humilitate, non elatione quaerenda et invenienda ostenderet. Oportet ergo, ut existimo, primum exponere quam quidem esse speculationem
headnotes.en: …desty of speech, that he might show that these things are to be sought and found by humility, not by elation. It behooves us, then, as I judge, first to set forth what indeed we reckon the speculation

headnotes.la: …singulae secundum ordines suos et dignitates in principatibus, et hierarchiis suis utilitatis accipiunt, quanto plus vel minus in laudem Creatoris per donum gratiae cooperantis assurgunt. Deinde, ait,
headnotes.en: …their orders and dignities in their principalities and hierarchies, so much of utility as they rise up, more or less, in the praise of the Creator through the gift of cooperating grace. Then, he says,

headnotes.la: Sequitur;
headnotes.en: There follows

headnotes.la: hoc est consequenter post ista supradicta, vel in consequentibus iis, qui sequuntur: Oportet
headnotes.en: that is, consequently after those things aforesaid, or in those things which follow: It behooves

headnotes.la: Hoc est enim, quod sequitur
headnotes.en: For this is what follows

headnotes.la: …olatilia, et caetera ad hunc modum. Et ne existimemus etiam quosdam illorum spirituum multorum vultuum esse, id est multos vultus sive facies habere, ut in Ezechiele scriptum est de animalibus sanctis
headnotes.en: …e rest in this manner. And lest we also suppose certain of those spirits to be many-faced, that is, to have many countenances or faces, as it is written in Ezekiel concerning the holy living creatures

headnotes.la: Sequitur
headnotes.en: There follows
